title: Normalization of a specified projective closure of an affine curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field, meaning that every algebraic extension of $k$ is separable [def-weil-field]. Let $U$ be an affine integral scheme of finite type over $k$ with $\dim U=1$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and fix a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow\mathbb A^n_k$ over $k$ for some $n\ge0$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-relative-affine-space]. Use the standard affine chart $D_+(T_0)\cong\mathbb A^n_k$ of $\mathbb P^n_k$ from the relative-Proj interface [def-nagata-relative-projective-space], with the same projective space over $k$ as in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and let $X$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of the composite immersion $U	o\mathbb P^n_k$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure]. Then $X$ is integral, projective over $k$, and of dimension one [def-kun-projective], and the factorization $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is a dense open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $
u:C=X^
u	o X$ be normalization in $k(X)$ [def-sc-normalization]. Then $C$ is integral, smooth, proper and of finite type over $k$, with $\dim C=1$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism]. The maps $j$ and $
u$ send generic points to generic points and induce $k$-isomorphisms $j^*:k(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(U)$ and $
u^*:k(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(C)$ of the generic stalks [def-sc-function-field]. Thus $j^*\circ(
u^*)^{-1}:k(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(U)$ is a $k$-isomorphism for these specified constructions.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (theorem-curves-rational-maps), final compactify-then-normalize alternative, and Tag 0BY3 (lemma-nonsingular-model-smooth). Reducedness of the actual scheme-theoretic closure: literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex, Tag 056B (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-reduced).

proof.text: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its only affine section ring is the field $k$, whose ideals are $0$ and $k$. Apply [det-nagata-affine-opens-projective] to the given affine $U$, finite-type structure morphism, and closed immersion $i$ (in particular an immersion). Its construction uses precisely the standard affine chart in the statement, so its $\overline U$ is the specified $X$. It gives projectivity, properness, and the dense open immersion $j:U\to X$. Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (theorem-curves-rational-maps), final compactify-then-normalize alternative; specified closure supplied by det-nagata-affine-opens-projective

proof.text: By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $U$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible. Apply [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] to $U\to\mathbb P^n_k$: the specified $X$ is reduced and its underlying space is the closure of the image of $U$. This closure is nonempty and irreducible: any two opens meeting it pull back to nonempty opens of $U$, whose intersection is nonempty. Thus $X$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme].
Apply [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension] to the integral finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ and its nonempty open $j(U)\cong U$. It gives $\dim X=\dim U=1$.

Apply [lem-sc-normalization-exists] to this $X$: $
u$ is finite and surjective, $C$ is proper, and $\dim C=\dim X=1$; properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Put $K=k(X)$ with generic point $\eta$. By [def-fin-normalization-extension] with $L=K$ (which is [def-sc-normalization]), every nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ has $
u^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}A'$, $A'$ the integral closure of $A$ in $K$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $A$ is a domain with fraction field $K$ (via germs), so $A\subseteq A'\subseteq K$ and $A'$ is a domain with fraction field $K$. So $
u^{-1}V$ is irreducible, nonempty ($
u$ surjective), with generic point $\xi_V=(0)$, and $
u(\xi_V)=\eta$ as $(0)\cap A=(0)$. If $V'\subseteq V$ are nonempty affine opens, the nonempty open $
u^{-1}V'$ of the irreducible $
u^{-1}V$ contains $\xi_V$, so $\xi_{V'}=\xi_V$. Any two nonempty affine opens of the irreducible $X$ contain a common one, so all $\xi_V$ are one point $\xi$, lying in every nonempty open of $C$. Hence $C$ is nonempty, irreducible and reduced (covered by spectra of domains): integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\xi$ over $\eta$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] for $C$ and $
u^{-1}V$, $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\xi}=\operatorname{Frac}A'$. The stalk map $
u^*:\mathcal O_{X,\eta}	o\mathcal O_{C,\xi}$ is compatible with the germ maps and $A\subseteq A'$, so it is the map $\operatorname{Frac}A	o\operatorname{Frac}A'$ induced by inclusion, i.e. the identity of $K$: an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 035H (definition-normalization-X-in-Y) and 0BXC (lemma-normalization-birational); affine description of normalization; generic stalk computation written out

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sc-normalized-curve-smooth] now hold: $X$ is integral, finite type over the perfect field $k$, and has dimension one. It gives smoothness of the specified $C=X^\nu$ over $k$.

By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], $U$ and $X$ have unique generic points. The generic point of $U$ belongs to every nonempty open of $U$; since $j(U)$ is dense open, its image meets every nonempty open of $X$, and is therefore the generic point of $X$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $U$ has the restricted structure sheaf of $X$. Opens contained in $j(U)$ are cofinal among neighbourhoods of its generic point, so the actual stalk map $j^*$ is an isomorphism: both stalks are the same colimit of sections on those neighbourhoods. This is the function-field map by [def-sc-function-field]. For $
u$, Step 4 showed that $
u$ sends the generic point $\xi$ of $C$ to the generic point $\eta$ of $X$ and that the generic-stalk map $
u^*:k(X)	o k(C)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 01RW (definition-function-field), 01RO (definition-birational) and 0BXC (lemma-normalization-birational); open-stalk argument from the definition of open immersion

proof.text:
Both morphisms are over $k$. On generic stalks, functoriality therefore gives $j^*(a\cdot1)=a\cdot1$ and $
u^*(a\cdot1)=a\cdot1$ for every $a\in k$. Applying the inverse of $
u^*$ gives the same equality for $(
u^*)^{-1}$. Consequently $j^*\circ(
u^*)^{-1}:k(C)	o k(U)$ is a $k$-isomorphism for these specified maps.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (theorem-curves-rational-maps), induced maps of function fields over k
